Commit: c1bf08ac ""ftrace: Be first to run code modification on modules""
changed ftrace module notifier's priority to INT_MAX in order to
process the ftrace nops before anything else could touch them
(namely kprobes). This was the correct thing to do.
Unfortunately
column2: the ftrace module notifier also contains the ftrace

column1: clean up code. As opposed to the set up code
run *after* all the module notifiers have run in case a module is doing
correct clean-up and unregisters its ftrace hooks. Basically
needs to do clean up on module removal
column2: as it needs to know about code

column1: being removed so that it doesn't try to modify that code. But after it
removes the module from its records
column2: if a ftrace user tries to remove

column1: a probe
column2: that removal will fail due as the record of that code segment

column1: no longer exists.
Nothing really bad happens if the probe removal is called after ftrace
did the clean up
column2: but the ftrace removal function will return an error.

column1: Correct code (such as kprobes) will produce a WARN_ON() if it fails
to remove the probe. As people get annoyed by frivolous warnings
best to do the ftrace clean up after everything else.
By splitting the ftrace_module_notifier into two notifiers
does the module load setup that is run at high priority
that is called for module clean up that is run at low priority
problem is solved.
